note_to_reader: These five notes have been through an editing pass. The other notes in each family are printed with them so a claim about a word's position on its family's spectrum can be checked against the words it is being compared with.

senses.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
senses.label: negative
senses.tone: Puts the fault in ordinariness rather than in damage - the thing is met everywhere rather than worn thin, which is what *threadbare* and *shopworn* make of the same overuse.
examples: his remarks were trite and commonplace
senses.axis: staleness held in contempt → plain absence of freshness

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: not original; not being or productive of something fresh and unusual
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The flat statement of the fault - nothing fresh in the thing and nothing fresh coming out of it - delivered without the scorn *trite* carries.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: Dismissal rather than description: the repetition has emptied the thing out, where *commonplace* only notes that it has been met before.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: A formal-sounding verdict that the thing has been run into the ground, heavier and more deliberate than *tired*.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: Informal and offhand: it shrugs at how familiar the thing has become instead of condemning it the way *banal* does.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The overuse leaves a mark, as though the thing had been handled until the shine came off it - grubbier than *well-worn*.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The flattest word here - it files the endless repetition almost as a category rather than a fault, with none of the disgust in *trite*.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The wear has gone all the way through: the thing still holds its shape but has nothing left in it, harsher than *well-worn*.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: Lays the wearing at time's door rather than at any user's: the overuse registers as accumulated age, not as the running-into-the-ground that *hackneyed* convicts someone of.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: Blunt and plain: the thing has simply gone slack from repetition, a flatter judgement than the arch *bromidic*.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The hardest word in the family - it does not merely note the overuse, it writes the thing off as worthless for it.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The gentlest of the group: the wear is admitted and half forgiven, where *threadbare* would call it ruin.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: Keeps a straight face while it convicts - dull, wearying and puffed up with significance, all named at once, where *corny* simply laughs.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: Informal and mocking: both the dullness and the airs come off as laughable, lighter on its feet than *platitudinous*.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The drier of the pair - it names the tiresome self-importance almost clinically, without the heavy roll of *platitudinous*.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: A weightier, more sonorous word than *platitudinal*, and its own bulk is part of the mockery: dullness dressed up and then shown up.

senses.label: neutral
senses.tone: Takes its smell from a wood, not from a spice, a fruit or a sweet, and names the tree whole where *balsam-scented* narrows to a resin.
senses.axis: a smell merely reported → a smell pinned to one named source

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: having odor or a characteristic odor
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The family's base term, covering both that a smell is present at all and that the thing has a smell of its own, and alone here it never says which smell.
Formal where the rest of the family is plain compounding, and it holds onion and garlic together rather than settling on either.
A flat identification of the source, describing the smell as almond's without any suggestion that this is welcome.
Names a licorice-sharp source where *almond-scented* names a softer one, though the word itself is equally free of praise or complaint.
Takes its smell from a fruit rather than a spice or a resin, and like every compound here it identifies without evaluating.
Fixes the smell to the resin rather than to the tree, making it the most exactly specified member of the family.
The one compound whose source is a made thing rather than a plant, and it names that smell with no verdict attached.
Warm where *mint-scented* is cool, though the warmth belongs to the spice and not to the compound, which identifies the smell as flatly as *clove-scented* names a sharper one.
Names the sharper of the two baking spices here, yet the word passes judgement no more than *cinnamon-scented* does.
Third of the kitchen spices in the family, labelling a smell by its source without hinting whether it pleases.
The sweetness sits in the source, not in the word, which reports it as flatly as *musk-scented* reports a heavier smell.
Borrows a fruit as *apple-scented* does, the sour one against the sweet, with neither compound taking a side.
Cool where *cinnamon-scented* is warm, but that contrast belongs to the sources named and not to anything the words themselves approve.
The one animal source among plants, spices and sweets, and the compound states it without the faintest verdict.
Carries the same sense as *musk-scented*, the -y form loosening the compound without changing what it identifies.

senses.definition: made to feel uncomfortable because of shame or wounded pride
senses.label: negative
senses.tone: Where *mortified* measures how sharp the discomfort is, this measures how far down it puts a person - shame or wounded pride, and no hand required to arrange the fall.
examples: humiliated that his wife had to go out to work
senses.axis: a passing inward discomfort → a public and settled loss of standing

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: feeling shame or guilt or embarrassment or remorse
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The plain inward word for the state, wide enough to hold guilt and remorse as well as shame, and unlike *disgraced* it reports the feeling without pronouncing on the person's standing.
The shame lands as a withdrawal of belief, where *disgraced* takes away the standing itself.
Total and public, the shame settled into a condition rather than the passing sting of *embarrassed*.
The gravest and most formal of these, shame weighed against honour, where *shamed* is blunt and unceremonious.
Bare and unadorned: shame worked on someone from outside, where *ashamed* is shame felt from within.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: made to feel uncomfortable because of shame or wounded pride
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: The mildest and most survivable discomfort here, and the sting can be to pride as easily as to conscience.

other_notes_in_this_family.gloss: made to feel uncomfortable because of shame or wounded pride
other_notes_in_this_family.tone: Hyperbolic in force: the discomfort is unbearable rather than merely awkward, and it can be pride that smarts.
The plainest of the words for guilt that shows, naming what is visible without the picture *hangdog* draws.
Contemptuous and pictorial, the guilt showing as a cowering, beaten posture, and the word relishes saying so.
Puts the guilt exactly where it shows, on the face, without the whole cringing body of *hangdog*.
Faintly comic and forgiving, the shame it shows small enough to be smiled at, where *hangdog* invites contempt.
